title_prefix: Data must be hexadecimal string omits Co
mechanism: Core's ParseOutputs parses a data output as ParseHexV(outputs[name_].getValStr(), "Data") (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/rawtransaction_util.cpp:113 at d3056bc), and ParseHexV (rpc/util.cpp:130-138) throws JSONRPCError(RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER, strprintf("%s must be hexadecimal string (not '%s')", name, strHex)) -- the offending value is echoed back in the message, and a non-string value yields the empty-string form "(not '')". Our parse-outputs wraps the hex decode in a handler-case and re-signals a fixed sentence with no suffix: src/rpc/amounts.lisp:131-139, the message literal at :135.
consequence: Message-shape divergence only; the output is rejected either way with the same code (-8) and the same leading sentence. It splits Core's own tests: rpc_rawtransaction.py:296 asserts only "Data must be hexadecimal string" and PASSES against us, while wallet_send.py:277 asserts "Data must be hexadecimal string (not 'Hello World')" and FAILS on the missing suffix, since assert_raises_rpc_error does a substring match. No client parses a wrong value and the error class is already correct, so S3. Worth noting the same omission is systemic rather than local: the sibling ParseHashV suffix forms that Core's tests assert -- "txid must be hexadecimal string (not '...')" (rpc_rawtransaction.py:271, rpc_txoutproof.py:61, mining_prioritisetransaction.py:219, wallet_basic.py:175), "blockhash must be hexadecimal string (not '...')" (rpc_blockchain.py:321, rpc_txoutproof.py:64, wallet_listsinceblock.py:95), "hash must be hexadecimal string (not '...')" (rpc_blockchain.py:454), "parameter 3 must be hexadecimal string (not '...')" (rpc_rawtransaction.py:167) and "txid must be of length 64 (not 3, for 'foo')" (rpc_rawtransaction.py:265) -- are all missing too; that wider absence is filed separately as adfc52aa.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3c, warm image. probe4.lisp called bl.rpc::dispatch-rpc-method "createrawtransaction" with outputs {"data": "Hello World"} and with {"data": "foo"}: both answer rpc-error -8 "Data must be hexadecimal string". probe9.lisp repeated the first through bl.rpc::handle-single-request: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-8,"message":"Data must be hexadecimal string"},"id":1} -- no "(not 'Hello World')". Tree grep confirms the literal exists once, at src/rpc/amounts.lisp:135, and that no " (not '" suffix is built anywhere in src/rpc/. Ours: src/rpc/amounts.lisp:131-139. Core at d3056bc: rpc/rawtransaction_util.cpp:113 and rpc/util.cpp:130-138 (ParseHexV), :117-125 (ParseHashV, the same suffix convention). Core functional tests: wallet_send.py:277 (full string, fails), rpc_rawtransaction.py:296 (prefix only, passes).
fix_shape: Introduce the missing Core primitive rather than patching the one string. Add parse-hex-v (and its sibling parse-hash-v) to src/rpc/amounts.lisp or the shared RPC helpers, taking the value and the argument NAME and signalling +rpc-invalid-parameter+ with exactly (format nil "~A must be hexadecimal string (not '~A')" name value) -- where value is the raw string as sent, and the empty string when the JSON value was not a string at all, matching ParseHexV's getValStr()/isStr() behaviour. Then call it from parse-outputs with the name "Data" so the data branch loses its handler-case entirely. Since this is the small half of adfc52aa, do the two together: the same helper gives getchaintxstats, getblockheader, gettxoutproof, prioritisetransaction, getrawtransaction's blockhash and createrawtransaction's txid Core's length form ("~A must be of length 64 (not ~D, for '~A')") and hex form in one place, which is also the only way the suffix stops being forgotten per call site. A regression test should assert the full wallet_send.py:277 string for a data output and one txid case with the length form.
